grammar_focus: could / was able to / managed to 的区别(could 表过去一般能力:he could climb any tree;was able to / managed to 表某一次成功做成:the firefighters were able to free him;could not 表过去做不到),外加“短语动词 + up”(save up / fill up / roll up / wrap up / button up / build up)(原创承载 NCE3 L15 考点·无需净化·美式改写:侄子 George 把硬币掉进下水道,胳膊卡住,消防队用润滑油救出,糖果店老板送他一大盒巧克力)
scene: 孩子们总是喜欢收到一点零花钱。爸爸妈妈会按时给零用,叔叔阿姨则是额外收入的来源。对有的孩子来说,几个硬币能花很久;对另一些孩子,一下午都撑不到。只有很节俭的孩子才攒得满一个储钱罐,摇起来硬币叮当作响。我侄子 George 也有个储钱罐,却总是空的——我给他的两毛五硬币几乎没一个落进去过。昨天我给了他五十美分,叫他攒起来,他却给自己买了“五十美分的麻烦”:去糖果店的路上,硬币掉在地上,顺着人行道弹了几下,滚进了下水道。George 脱下外套,卷起袖子,把胳膊从下水道盖的缝里伸了进去。硬币没摸着,更糟的是胳膊也抽不出来了。人群围了上来,一位好心女士往他胳膊上抹黄油,可他还是死死卡住。最后消防队来了,忙了将近一个钟头,两名消防员用一点润滑油把他救了出来。George 倒没怎么沮丧——糖果店的老板娘听说了这事,送了他一大盒巧克力。

grammar_card.title: could / was able to / managed to + 短语动词 up
grammar_card.intro: ①could 表示“过去的一般能力”(以前一直会/能):When he was little, he could climb any tree。②但表示“某一次终于做成、成功办到”时,不用 could,而用 was/were able to 或 managed to:After an hour, the firefighters were able to free him(= managed to free him)。③could not / couldn't 表示“过去做不到”:He could not pull his arm out。④“短语动词 + up”很常见:save up(攒钱)、fill up(装满)、roll up(卷起)、wrap up(包起)、button up(扣好)、build up(积累)、eat up(吃光)。

rows: They were able to free him. / He managed to escape.
He could not pull his arm out.
save up / fill up / roll up / wrap up

specialRules.rule: 肯定句里“某一次终于办到”不能用 could,要用 was able to / managed to;could 只用于“过去一般能力”或否定句 could not。
could not 是过去“做不到”:He could not find it（找不到）。别写成 could not to。
up 常与动词搭成短语:save up 攒起来、fill up 装满、roll up 卷起、button up 扣好。美语里“零花钱”说 allowance(英式 pocket money),“人行道”说 sidewalk(英式 pavement),“糖果”说 candy(英式 sweets)。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Did George get anything for his fifty cents in the end?
options: Yes, a big box of chocolates

passage: Kids always appreciate small gifts of money. Mom and dad hand out a regular allowance, of course, but uncles and aunts are a welcome source of extra cash. To some kids a few coins go a long way; to others they never last an afternoon. Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a piggy bank, and when they shake it, the coins rattle happily inside. My nephew, George, has a piggy bank, but it is always empty. Almost none of the quarters I have given him ever find their way in. Yesterday I gave him fifty cents and told him to save it up. Instead, he bought himself fifty cents' worth of trouble. On his way to the candy store, George dropped the coin. It bounced along the sidewalk and disappeared down a drain. George could always squeeze his hand into tight spaces, so he took off his jacket, rolled up his sleeves, and pushed his arm through the drain cover. He could not find the coin, and worse, he could not pull his arm back out. A crowd gathered, and a kind woman rubbed his arm with butter, but George was stuck fast. At last the fire department was called, and after nearly an hour two firefighters were able to free him with a little grease. George was not upset for long: the woman who owns the candy store heard about it all and rewarded him with a big box of chocolates.

stage5.stem: "After an hour, two firefighters ___ free George from the drain."(某一次成功做成,不用 could)

stage5.stem: "Please ___ the gift nicely before the party."(短语动词“包起来”)

stage5.stem: "It's cold, so ___ your coat before you go out."(短语动词“扣好”)
stage5.stem_cn: 天冷,出门前把外套扣好。

stage5.stem: "A person who saves money carefully and spends little is ___."(“节俭的”用哪个词)

stage5.stem: "When a ball hits the ground and jumps back up, it ___."(“弹起”用哪个词)
